headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Authelia can forward-auth/OIDC traffic while Plano ingests chat-completion inputs and logs, creating a plausible shared-data path without direct evidence of a dangerous default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, while Plano consumes OpenAI-compatible chat completions and config files. No shared channel or parser is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced; the only plausible bridge is manual or operator-mediated content flow, which keeps blast radius limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies Authelia-generated text into Plano prompts or config files
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between Authelia and Plano
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into Plano prompts
Add a provenance label to any Authelia output before reuse
Review config.yaml changes before applying them
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia can handle authentication traffic and has broad network egress; Plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. A shared workspace or forwarded request context could leak sensitive auth material into Plano’s telemetry or outbound API calls. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Authelia request/identity data is forwarded into Plano prompts, logs, or traces
IF Plano sends those logs or prompts to a third-party inference API
mitigations: Do not route authentication payloads into Plano
Redact tokens and identifiers before logging
Turn off verbose request logging in Plano
Restrict Plano to non-sensitive test traffic
requires-engineering: isolate telemetry pipelines per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, subprocess spawning, or overlapping mutable resource control. Plano explicitly does not support multiple instances, which reduces concurrency risk rather than creating a write conflict. The interaction is therefore limited and mostly operational.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API quota or shared OAuth principal
IF an operator gives both write access to the same mutable backend
mitigations: Use separate API keys per agent
Avoid shared writable databases
Run only one Plano instance per deployment
Document ownership of each external resource
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit auth decisions via OIDC/ForwardAuth, and Plano can consume chat-completion inputs and produce logs/traces. If Authelia-derived output is treated as authoritative by Plano, errors can cascade into downstream responses or routing decisions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Plano uses Authelia output as prompt context or policy input without validation
IF downstream systems act on Plano outputs derived from that context
mitigations: Insert a human review step for policy-sensitive outputs
Validate Authelia-derived fields before reuse
Keep auth decisions separate from generation prompts
Log source provenance for every forwarded field
requires-engineering: add schema validation and allowlists

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service and Plano handles logs, traces, and metrics, but neither profile states regulated data classes, residency, or certification mismatches. Because the compliance pathway is undocumented and no PHI/EU PII is evidenced, only a low residual compliance risk is supportable.
conditions: IF regulated identity data is stored in Plano logs or traces
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not configured here
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Plano telemetry
Set short log-retention windows
Review data-processing agreements before production use
Separate auth records from analytics data
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls
